explanation: A daguerreotype was a one-off image on a silvered copper plate. Talbot's paper negative could be printed again and again, the basis of film photography for over 150 years.

claims.text: Talbot's calotype process, patented in 1841, produced a paper negative from which many positive prints could be made, unlike the daguerreotype.
The calotype did not give sharper detail than the daguerreotype, and it produced neither full colour nor instant prints.
A daguerreotype was a unique image on a silver-coated copper plate that could not be reproduced as a print.
The negative-positive principle of the calotype was the basis of film photography for more than 150 years.
